title: Best Practices to Clean Ultrathin Carbon and Graphene Film Grids for TEM Analysis
content: The optimized removal of hydrocarbon contamination from transmission electron microscopy (TEM) ultrathin carbon and graphene grids [1] for high-resolution imaging and micro-analysis is the focus of this work. This study proposes to systematically evaluate plasma cleaning protocols using Hydrogen-Nitrogen mixtures in order to avoid degradation of both the sample being studied and the carbon-based support grid. We will compare this gas chemistry to the more conventional plasma cleaning gases such as room air and Forming gas with particular emphasis on preserving the structural integrity and oxidation state of the sample and their support films. We also plan to investigate if these plasma cleaning processes maintain the hydrophilic properties of the grid surface [2].
